A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material. All 25 pages were compared; the supplementary pages have identical text and rendered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on synthetic and real faces, THuman 2.1, 2K2K, and ClearPose, together with ablations and supplementary subspace analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, quantitative results, qualitative reconstructions, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The controlled synthetic-data generation, LoRA ensemble construction, reweighted least-squares/SVD subspace extraction, and subspace-based VGGT fine-tuning procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is unchanged. The added Section 5 overview sentence mentions transparent-object reconstruction, but ClearPose evaluation already appears in v1 Section 5.3 and Table 3.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: VGGT, full fine-tuning, LoRA, and PiSSA for faces and humans; VGGT, full fine-tuning, LoRA, and AdaLoRA for ClearPose. The principal-singular-vector ablation is also retained.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, metrics, input views, ranks, and training settings are unchanged. Both versions retain eight-view human evaluation and the ClearPose split using 32 of 51 scenes for training.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same subspace spectral and orthogonality analyses, principal-singular-vector and LoRA-rank ablations, and supplementary rank-allocation comparisons and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version provides repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the benchmark scores.

E6.justification: Table 2 corrects a displayed ranking: LoRA (rank 64)'s THuman completeness score of 1.902 changes from bold best-result marking to underlined second-best marking, consistent with Ours (d=64) scoring 1.882. All numerical values, result entries, and qualitative findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The optimization objectives, reweighted least-squares/SVD derivation, subspace-distance and generalized-eigenvalue formulations, and supplementary effective-rank definition are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about attribute-specific subspaces, approximate disentanglement, efficient fine-tuning, and transfer from synthetic to real data. Transparent-object evaluation was already included in the introduction.

C2.justification: The new overview sentence summarizes the existing ClearPose evaluation as demonstrating effectiveness with complex materials and limited training data. The substantive generalization discussion, mechanism explanations, and limitations, including static-scene scope and fine-detail reconstruction difficulties, are unchanged.

D1.justification: Supplementary implementation and data-generation details are identical, including the VGGT-1B checkpoint, learning-rate schedule, gradient clipping, 24,000 training steps, approximately 20 hours on an H200 GPU, and rendering procedures. No access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Related-work discussion and cited works are unchanged in both the main text and supplement. The MegaSynth reference's page locator changes because its citation moves during reflow.

P1.justification: Section 5 slightly rephrases the synthetic-to-real generalization sentence and adds an overview sentence covering the existing transparent-object experiment. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; section organization is retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 changes the 1.902 completeness entry from bold to underlined. The expanded overview also causes local text, caption, and table-spacing adjustments on pages 5–7. No figures or tables are added or removed, and supplementary layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects misleading best-result highlighting in Table 2 and makes the experimental overview cover the already-reported ClearPose evaluation. These provide modest gains in reporting accuracy and clarity; the methods, numerical evidence, and supplementary material remain unchanged.
